APRS101 rain-gauge example: trailing text as software/unit. Source: APRS101 pp. 63-64 (profile core-1.1). The specification's own example. By the p.63 layout a report ends with the optional software code S (1 byte) and unit code uuuu (2-4 bytes), so the trailing 'Jim' is software 'J' and unit 'im'. The grammar cannot distinguish a short name from these codes.

Short trailing text reads as software/unit codes. Source: APRS101 p. 63 (profile core-1.1). Unit codes are open-ended ('Users may specify any other 2-4 character code'), so any 3-5 trailing characters that end the report are read as S plus uuuu. Receivers must not reinterpret them as comment text.

Text after software/unit codes is comment. Source: APRS101 pp. 63-66 (profile core-1.1). Every weather format ends with the optional S and uuuu codes; none defines a comment after them. Text that does not end the report as exactly those codes is retained as comment and no codes are inferred. Transmitters must not place a comment after the codes.

comment: Positioned weather with a north wind (0 degrees) at 1 mph: APRS101 p. 27 gives the direction as 001-360 (000/000 is the unavailable pair), so north is sent as 360/001 and reads back as 360, the same direction.

Weather station sending the time of day 17:47:06 with a 'z' suffix (as in live APN390 traffic, e.g. TRF-00172): read as day/hour/minute, hour 47 is invalid. The position and weather stay usable, so they decode with the timestamp left out and a nonconforming diagnostic; FAP does the same with a warning. Differs from FAP: FAP reports 000/000 wind as 0 degrees at 0 speed; APRS101 p. 28: 000/000 means unknown wind, so here it is unavailable.

diagnostics.message: must be in 0..23; timestamp '174706z' not decoded

comment: Compressed position with symbol /W followed by weather fields: csT course/speed is wind. Differs from FAP (representation only): FAP reports compressed csT under a weather symbol as course/speed; here it is the wind (APRS101 p. 39). /W and \W are weather symbols, interchangeable with _ (aprs.org/aprs11/spec-wx.txt), so a course/speed under W is wind. Reading it as station motion when no weather field follows is the opt-in reinterpretive extension w_symbol_motion. Differs from FAP: FAP does not treat /W and \W as weather symbols.

Live APRS-IS weather (originally TRF-00422 in the full capture) with wind 000/001. Decision: APRS101 p. 27 gives the wind direction as 001-360, with 000/000 the unavailable pair, so a 000 direction with a non-zero speed decodes as 0 degrees (north) with a nonconforming diagnostic, and north is sent as 360. Weather fields are re-sent in canonical order.

diagnostics.message: wind direction 000 is outside 001-360; north is sent as 360

comment: Symbol /W with wind 180/010 and rain r001 but no gust or temperature, under the default policy (PR #6 review, item 3): a weather field follows, so it is an incomplete weather report, diagnosed and refused when sent. /W and \W are weather symbols, interchangeable with _ (aprs.org/aprs11/spec-wx.txt). Differs from FAP: FAP reads the course/speed under /W as motion; here /W is a weather symbol, interchangeable with _ (aprs.org/aprs11/spec-wx.txt), so the pair is wind (motion only with the opt-in w_symbol_motion). Differs from FAP: FAP does not treat /W and \W as weather symbols; here they are, as spec-wx (aprs.org/aprs11/spec-wx.txt) accepts them interchangeably with _.
